_note: Source document for translators. Never read at runtime - the English shown by the plugin is compiled into the call sites, so this file cannot disagree with what is drawn. Regenerate it rather than editing it by hand.

sharecodes.heading.description: Heading for the share-code row, which sits at the bottom of the Presets tab.

sharecodes.intro.message: A code is the whole preset as one line of text. Paste one into chat to hand it to someone.
sharecodes.intro.description: Explains what a share code is. "Chat" means the game's chat window.

sharecodes.copy.description: Button. Puts a code for the settings as they stand onto the clipboard.

sharecodes.copied.message: Copied. Paste it wherever you like.
sharecodes.copied.description: Confirmation shown for a few seconds after the copy button is pressed.

sharecodes.copy.tooltip.named.message:
Puts a code for everything as it stands right now on the clipboard,
under the name "{0}".
sharecodes.copy.tooltip.named.description: Tooltip on the copy button once a name has been typed. Keep the line break. {0} is the name the player typed, so keep the quotes around it. sharecodes.customfont.note may be appended after this.

sharecodes.copy.tooltip.unnamed.message:
Type a name in the box above first: it travels with the code, and it
is all the person you send it to will have to go on.

To share a preset you have already saved, right-click it instead.
sharecodes.copy.tooltip.unnamed.description: Tooltip on the copy button while it is disabled for want of a name. Keep the line breaks.

sharecodes.paste.description: Button. Reads a code from the clipboard and applies it.

sharecodes.paste.tooltip.named.message:
Reads a code from the clipboard, saves it as one of your presets, and
applies it. It will be filed under "{0}" rather than
the name the code arrived with.
sharecodes.paste.tooltip.named.description: Tooltip on the paste button once a name has been typed. Keep the line breaks. {0} is the name the player typed, so keep the quotes around it.

sharecodes.paste.tooltip.unnamed.message:
Reads a code from the clipboard, saves it as one of your presets, and
applies it under the name it arrived with.

Type a name above first to file it under that instead.
sharecodes.paste.tooltip.unnamed.description: Tooltip on the paste button when no name has been typed. Keep the line breaks.

sharecodes.clipboard.unreadable.message: Could not read the clipboard. Try again in a moment.
sharecodes.clipboard.unreadable.description: Shown when the clipboard cannot be read at all, which is usually another program holding it open.

sharecodes.imported.description: Shown after a code is pasted successfully. {0} is the preset's name - keep the quotes. A further sentence may be appended after this one when the code needs a font the player does not have.

about.tab.description: Tab label. Short - it sits in a row of tabs and a long word pushes the others off.

about.title.description: Heading at the top of the About tab. "Regions of XIV" is the plugin's name and stays as-is; {0} is the version number.

about.author.description: Sits under the title. {0} is the author's name and is never translated - it is passed in separately so it cannot be.

about.summary.message: Announces the region, zone, area and sub-area you walk into, and the weather while you are there, replacing the game's own location text rather than drawing alongside it.
about.summary.description: One-paragraph description of what the plugin does. "Region", "zone", "area" and "sub-area" are the four tiers of place name the plugin announces; the same four words appear on the Announcements tab, so keep them consistent.

about.whatsnew.description: Button opening the changelog window. Keep it short - four buttons share one row and wrap when they do not fit.

about.whatsnew.tooltip.message: Every release, newest first. Also at "/regions changelog".
about.whatsnew.tooltip.description: Tooltip for the What's new button. "/regions changelog" is a command typed into the game and is never translated.

about.discord.description: Button opening the project's Discord invite. Keep it short - four buttons share one row.

about.discord.tooltip.message: Ideas, bug reports and preset codes.
about.discord.tooltip.description: Tooltip for the Discord button. The address it opens is appended automatically by common.opens.

about.github.description: Button opening the source repository. "GitHub" is a product name and stays as-is.

about.github.tooltip.message: The source, the releases, and the licence.

about.issue.description: Button opening the bug tracker. Keep it short - four buttons share one row.

about.issue.tooltip.description: Tooltip for the Report an issue button.

about.commands.description: Heading above the list of chat commands.

about.command.settings.description: What "/regions" does. The command itself is not translated.

about.command.test.message: Shows a notification for where you are standing.
about.command.test.description: What "/regions test" does. The command itself is not translated.

about.command.changelog.description: What "/regions changelog" does. "What's New" is that window's title - match about.whatsnew.

about.inspiration.message: Inspired by Nekres' Regions of Tyria for Guild Wars 2.
about.inspiration.description: Credit line, clickable. "Nekres" is a person's name, "Regions of Tyria" is their addon and "Guild Wars 2" is a game - none of the three are translated.

about.inspiration.tooltip.description: Tooltip on the credit line. {0} is a web address.

about.licence.description: "AGPL-3.0-or-later" is the licence's formal identifier and stays exactly as it is.

about.notaffiliated.message: Place names, weather and fonts come from the game's own data. Not affiliated with Square Enix.
about.notaffiliated.description: Legal note at the foot of the tab. "Square Enix" is a company name and stays as-is.

presets.tab.description: Tab label. Short - it sits in a row of tabs and a long word pushes the others off.

presets.intro.message: A preset covers Announcements, Appearance, Motion and Fonts: the face and size of each line, position, colours, motion and particles, which tiers announce, the timings, and when to stay quiet. Sound is not included.
presets.intro.description: Paragraph at the top of the tab. Announcements, Appearance, Motion and Fonts are the names of four other tabs in this window - match how you translated each tab's own label. Sound is a fifth tab, named here because a preset deliberately leaves it alone.

presets.intro.warning.message: Applying one replaces all of them, so anything you have changed is overwritten.

presets.builtin.description: Heading over the row of presets that ship with the plugin.

presets.builtin.hint.message: The defaults, plus the look each one is named for.
presets.builtin.hint.description: Greyed line under the Built-in looks heading.

presets.builtin.tooltip.message:
{0}
Everything else returns to its default.
presets.builtin.tooltip.description: Tooltip on each built-in preset button. {0} is that preset's own description, one of the presets.*.description entries below. Keep the line break.

presets.classic.description.message: The plugin as it ships: a decode, no movement, no particles.
presets.classic.description.description: Describes the Classic preset. The preset NAMES themselves are never translated - they travel inside share codes, so a preset saved as "Classic" has to arrive as "Classic" on someone else's machine. Only these descriptions are.

presets.inferno.description.message: Letters catch alight and cool into place, embers rising off them.
presets.inferno.description.description: Describes the Inferno preset. "Embers" is also a Particles entry - match motion.particles.embers.

presets.sweetheart.description.message: Letters lift into place with hearts drifting up around them.
presets.sweetheart.description.description: Describes the Sweetheart preset. "Hearts" is also a Particles entry - match motion.particles.hearts.

presets.starlight.description.message: The line rides a wave in, sparkles hanging in the air around it.
presets.starlight.description.description: Describes the Starlight preset. "Wave" and "Sparkles" are dropdown entries - match motion.choice.wave and motion.particles.sparkles.

presets.sakura.description.message: A gentle rise under falling petals.
presets.sakura.description.description: Describes the Sakura preset. "Rise" and "Petals" are dropdown entries - match motion.choice.rise and motion.particles.petals.

presets.dispatch.description.message: Typed out one letter at a time, in tight uppercase. No particles.
presets.dispatch.description.description: Describes the Dispatch preset. Refers to the Typewriter motion - match motion.choice.typewriter if you name it.

presets.tyria.description.message: Wide uppercase in gold, still and unhurried. A nod to the original.
presets.tyria.description.description: Describes the Tyria preset. "The original" means Regions of Tyria, the Guild Wars 2 addon this plugin is modelled on.

presets.saved.description: Heading over the presets the player has saved themselves.

presets.saved.hint.message: Your settings, saved exactly as they were.
presets.saved.hint.description: Greyed line under the Your presets heading.

presets.saved.none.message: You have not saved any yet.
presets.saved.none.description: Shown in place of the list when the player has saved no presets.

presets.saved.tooltip.message:
Apply this preset.
Right-click to share, overwrite or delete it.
presets.saved.tooltip.description: Tooltip on each saved preset button. Keep the line break.

presets.menu.share.description: Right-click menu entry on a saved preset.

presets.menu.overwrite.description: Right-click menu entry on a saved preset.

presets.menu.delete.description: Right-click menu entry on a saved preset.

presets.copied.description: Confirmation after copying a saved preset's share code. {0} is that preset's name - keep the quotes.

presets.name.hint.message: Name it to save, copy or import
presets.name.hint.description: Placeholder text inside the empty name box. Keep it short; the box is about 180 pixels wide.

presets.save.description: Button beside the name box, shown when the typed name is not in use yet.

presets.replace.description: The same button as presets.save, shown instead when the typed name matches a preset that already exists.

presets.save.tooltip.message: Saves every setting on Announcements, Appearance, Motion and Fonts. Sound is not included.
presets.save.tooltip.description: Tooltip on the Save/Replace button. The four names are other tabs in this window - match their labels. Sound is a fifth, excluded on purpose.

presets.discord.description: Button at the foot of the tab. The About tab has its own button with the same wording under about.discord, so each can be worded to fit its context.

presets.discord.tooltip.message: Trade preset codes, report a bug, or suggest a feature.
presets.discord.tooltip.description: Tooltip for the Discord button on this tab. The address it opens is appended automatically by common.opens.

presets.customfont.warning.message: These settings use a font from this PC. A preset stores where that file sits, not the font itself, so on anyone else's machine the path will not exist and those lines fall back to Noto Sans CJK. Everything else in the preset still applies. Put the line back on a built-in face if you want a preset to look the same for whoever you hand it to.
presets.customfont.warning.description: Warning shown above the save row when the current settings use a font file from the player's own PC. "Noto Sans CJK" is a font name and stays as-is.

presets.customfont.missing.message: It carries a font file from the sender's PC that is not on yours, so those lines are drawn with Noto Sans CJK. Choose your own on the Fonts tab.
presets.customfont.missing.description: Appended to sharecodes.imported when an imported code wants a font the player does not have. "Fonts" is a tab in this window - match its label. "Noto Sans CJK" is a font name and stays as-is.

fonts.tab.description: Tab label. Short - it sits in a row of tabs and a long word pushes the others off.

fonts.intro.message: Every line of a notification has its own face and size. Pick one of the built-in faces, or point the plugin at a font file on this PC.
fonts.intro.description: Paragraph at the top of the tab. "Face" here means typeface.

fonts.role.text.description: Inner tab label for the largest line of a notification, the place name. Keep it short - three of these sit in one row.

fonts.role.text.hint.message: The place name itself, the largest line.
fonts.role.text.hint.description: Greyed line under the Text tab.

fonts.role.header.description: Inner tab label for the smaller line above the place name. Keep it short.

fonts.role.header.hint.message: The smaller line above the name, giving the region or area it sits in.
fonts.role.header.hint.description: Greyed line under the Header tab. "Region" and "area" are two of the place tiers - match announcements.zone and announcements.area.

fonts.role.weather.description: Inner tab label for the forecast line. Keep it short.

fonts.role.weather.hint.message: The forecast line above the header, shown when weather announcements are on.
fonts.role.weather.hint.description: Greyed line under the Weather tab.

fonts.size.description: Slider label, shown once per role tab.

fonts.face.description: Dropdown label for choosing the typeface, shown once per role tab.

fonts.face.tooltip.message:
Noto Sans CJK is vector: sharp at any size, and it covers every language.

The game's own faces suit FFXIV better, but each is a bitmap with a ceiling:
Trump Gothic: Latin only, to 91 px.
Jupiter: Latin only, to 61 px.
Axis: to 48 px, the only one with Japanese glyphs.

Custom file loads a font of your own from this PC.
fonts.face.tooltip.description: Tooltip for the font dropdown. Keep the line breaks. "Noto Sans CJK", "Trump Gothic", "Jupiter" and "Axis" are names of typefaces and are never translated. "Custom file" is a dropdown entry - match fonts.choice.custom. "px" is the pixel abbreviation.

fonts.choice.noto.description: Dropdown entry. {0} is the typeface name "Noto Sans CJK", passed in separately so it cannot be translated by accident. Only "(recommended)" is yours to translate.

fonts.choice.custom.description: Dropdown entry for using a font file from the player's own PC. The other entries in this dropdown are typeface names and are not translated.

fonts.preview.description: Button that fires a sample notification, one per role tab. The Motion and Appearance tabs have their own with the same wording and their own keys.

fonts.path.hint.description: Placeholder text inside the empty font-path box. The three extensions are file types and stay as they are.

fonts.browse.description: Button opening a file picker. Keep it short - it shares a row with the path box and Clear.

fonts.browse.tooltip.message: Opens your Windows font folder. Any .ttf, .otf or .ttc file will do.

fonts.clear.description: Button that empties the font path. Keep it short - it shares a row with the path box and Browse.

fonts.dialog.title.description: Title of the file picker window opened by Browse.

fonts.drawingwith.description: Confirms which custom font file is in use. {0} is a file name.

fonts.custom.notice.message: A font you supply is loaded exactly as it is, and it stays yours to look after. Missing glyphs, odd spacing, soft edges, a file the game cannot read, or a licence you do not hold are on you rather than on Regions of XIV, and no support is offered for anything that comes of one. If a line stops looking right, put it back on one of the built-in faces.
fonts.custom.notice.description: Warning shown whenever a custom font is selected. "Regions of XIV" is the plugin's name and stays as-is. This one disclaims responsibility, so keep it plain and keep its meaning exactly.

fonts.nojapanese.message: {0} has no Japanese glyphs. On this client that means place names will render as blank boxes, not just look soft. Choose Axis or Noto Sans CJK instead.
fonts.nojapanese.description: Shown on a Japanese client when a Latin-only typeface is picked. {0} is that typeface's name. "Axis" and "Noto Sans CJK" are typeface names and stay as-is.

fonts.upscaled.message: This font has no bitmap above {0:F0} px, so at {1:F0} px it is being upscaled and will look soft. Lower the size, or switch to Noto Sans CJK or a font file of your own, either of which stays sharp at any size.
fonts.upscaled.description: Shown when the chosen size exceeds what a bitmap typeface holds. {0} is the largest size it has, {1} is the size chosen - keep the ":F0" inside both braces, it rounds them to whole numbers. "px" is the pixel abbreviation.

command.help.message: Open the Regions of XIV settings. "{0}" fires a sample notification, "{1}" shows what has changed.
command.help.description: Shown in Dalamud's own list of chat commands. {0} and {1} are the commands themselves, "/regions test" and "/regions changelog" - they are what the player types, so never translate them, and keep the quotation marks around them. "Regions of XIV" is the plugin's name.

changelog.title.description: Title bar of the What's New window. "Regions of XIV" is the plugin's name and stays as-is; only the second half is translated. Match about.whatsnew, which is the button that opens this window.

changelog.all.description: Line at the top of the window when the player opened it themselves, above the full list.

changelog.updated.message: Regions of XIV has updated. Here is what changed:
changelog.updated.description: Line at the top when the window opened itself after an update and there is exactly one release to show. "Regions of XIV" is the plugin's name.

changelog.updated.away.message: Regions of XIV has updated. Here is what changed while you were away:
changelog.updated.away.description: The same line when more than one release is being shown at once, because the player skipped some updates. "Regions of XIV" is the plugin's name.

changelog.discord.description: Button opening the project's Discord invite. "Discord" is a product name and stays as-is. The same words appear on the Presets and About tabs; they are separate entries because each button needs its own identity, but they should read the same.

changelog.discord.tooltip.message:
Ideas, bug reports and preset codes.
{0}
changelog.discord.tooltip.description: Tooltip for the Join the Discord button. {0} is the invite address - keep it on its own line.

changelog.onceonly.message: You will not see this again until the next update.
changelog.onceonly.description: Footer shown when the window opened itself after an update.

changelog.onrequest.description: Footer shown when the player opened the window themselves. {0} is the command they typed; it is never translated, and the quotes around it stay.

window.editing.description: Checkbox above the row of tabs, which holds a sample notification on screen while the player changes settings.

window.editing.tooltip.message:
Keeps one sample notification on screen while you work, instead of
starting a new one every time you change something.

Zone announcements are held back while this is on. It switches itself
off when you close this window.
window.editing.tooltip.description: Tooltip for the Editing mode checkbox. Keep the line breaks, including the blank line between the two paragraphs.

window.discord.description: Tooltip on the speech-bubble button in this window's title bar. {0} is the invite address - keep it on its own line. "Discord" is a product name and stays as-is.

common.opens.description: Wraps every link button's tooltip. {0} is the sentence about that button, {1} is the web address it opens. Keep the blank line between them.

common.colour.tooltip.message:
Currently {0:F0}% solid.

Click for the full picker. The narrow chequered strip right of the rainbow is alpha (how solid this colour is) and it stops at {1:F0}%, far enough back to sit behind the other lines but not so far that the line disappears and looks like a fault.
common.colour.tooltip.description: Tooltip shown on every colour swatch in this window. {0} is how solid the colour currently is and {1} is the lowest it can go, both as percentages - keep the ":F0" inside the braces, it rounds them to whole numbers, and keep the per-cent signs after them. "Alpha" is the usual word for how solid a colour is; use whatever a painting or image program says in your language. Keep the blank line after the first sentence.

units.px.description: Unit shown after the number on a slider, as in "12 px". The abbreviation for pixels. A space is added before it in code, so do not start this with one.

units.lines.description: Unit shown after the number on the Header gap and Banner drop sliders, as in "1.50 lines". Both are measured in lines of text. A space is added before it in code, so do not start this with one.

units.seconds.description: Unit shown after the number on every duration slider, as in "0.35 s". The abbreviation for seconds - keep it short, it sits inside a narrow slider. A space is added before it in code, so do not start this with one.

units.times.description: Unit shown after the number on the particle Density slider, as in "1.5x", meaning a multiplier. No space is added before this one, so it sits against the number.

presetcode.empty.message: There is nothing on the clipboard to import.
presetcode.empty.description: Shown when Paste a code is pressed with an empty clipboard. These presetcode.* messages appear in red under the buttons on the Presets tab, and only ever when something has gone wrong - keep them plain and say what the player should do.

presetcode.toolong.message: That code is too long to be one of ours.
presetcode.toolong.description: The clipboard held far more text than any share code contains, so it is almost certainly something else entirely.

presetcode.notacode.message: That does not look like a preset code. They start with "{0}".
presetcode.notacode.description: The text does not begin with the marker every code starts with. {0} is that marker - currently "ROX1-", including the trailing dash. It is part of the code format, so never translate it, and keep the quotes around it.

presetcode.unreadable.message: That code did not unpack to anything readable.
presetcode.unreadable.description: The code had the right shape but the compressed data inside it was not valid.

presetcode.notapreset.message: That code did not unpack to a preset.
presetcode.notapreset.description: The code unpacked into readable data, but that data was not a preset.

presetcode.noname.message: That code carries no preset name.
presetcode.noname.description: A code always travels with a name for the preset, and this one had none.

presetcode.damaged.message: That code is damaged. Some of it went missing on the way here. Ask for it again and copy the whole line in one go.
presetcode.damaged.description: Much the most common failure: the player copied only part of a code, because chat wrapped it across lines. That specific claim - part of the code is missing, and the fix is to copy the whole line at once - is the whole point of the message, so keep it rather than smoothing it into a general "could not read that code".

sharecodes.customfont.note.message:
The code carries a font file from this PC. Whoever you send it to will
not have that file, so those lines fall back to Noto Sans CJK for them.
sharecodes.customfont.note.description: Appended to sharecodes.copy.tooltip.named when the settings use a font file from this PC. Keep the two blank lines at the start - they separate it from the sentence before. "Noto Sans CJK" is a font name and stays as-is.

notice.dismiss.description: Button that hides the notice above for this language. Short - it sits directly under the notice.

notice.translation.message:
This translation was drafted by a machine and has not been checked by anyone who speaks the language. If something reads badly, corrections are very welcome:
{0}
notice.translation.description: Shown at the top of the settings window when the loaded translation marks itself a machine draft. {0} is the Discord invite address - keep it on its own line. This one matters more than most: it is the only thing telling a reader that what they are looking at has not been checked, so it needs to be plain and unmistakable in your language.

fonts.reduced.message: Drawing at {0:F0} px rather than {1:F0}. This client shows Japanese place names, so every notification font has to carry kanji, and at that size it would be too large to build. Your setting is kept as it is and comes back if the game's language changes.
fonts.reduced.description: Shown under the size slider when the stored size is larger than this client can build. It only appears on a Japanese client, and only for someone whose config was set while the game was in another language. {0} is the size actually used and {1} the size they asked for; keep the ":F0" inside both braces, it rounds them to whole numbers. The reassurance in the last sentence matters: nothing has been rewritten, so say so plainly.

sound.browse.description: Button opening a file picker. Matches the Browse button on the Fonts tab, so use the same word you used there.

sound.clear.description: Button emptying the chosen sound file path. Matches Clear on the Fonts tab.

sound.custom.notice.message: A file you supply is played as it is, and it stays yours to look after. Anything past {0} seconds is cut off, so a whole track will not play over a notification that has already gone. A file the plugin cannot read, or one you do not hold a licence for, is on you rather than on Regions of XIV.
sound.custom.notice.description: A caution under the file row. {0} is a number of seconds, currently 5. It is the plugin's own disclaimer about a file the player supplied, so keep it plain rather than legalistic.

sound.dialog.title.description: Title bar of the file picker.

sound.path.hint.description: Placeholder text inside an empty path box. ".wav" and ".mp3" are file extensions and stay as they are.

sound.play.description: Button that plays the chosen file straight away so the player can hear what they picked.

sound.play.tooltip.message: Plays the chosen file now. It ignores the short gap that stops two notifications sounding at once, so pressing it repeatedly always tries again.
sound.play.tooltip.description: Tooltip for that button. The "short gap" is a quarter of a second that stops two notifications arriving together from making two overlapping sounds.

sound.playingwith.description: Shown under the path box when the file is usable. {0} is the file's name, not its full path.

sound.problem.channels.message: That file has more than two channels, which cannot be played here. A mono or stereo file will work.
sound.problem.channels.description: The file has more than two channels, meaning surround sound. The plugin plays mono and stereo only.

sound.problem.decode.message: That file could not be read. The plugin's log names the format it saw, which is the quickest way to see why.
sound.problem.decode.description: The file could not be decoded. It is a .wav or .mp3 by name but not one the plugin can read, either because it is damaged or because it uses an unusual encoding.

sound.problem.device.message: Windows would not open an audio device, so nothing can be played.
sound.problem.device.description: Windows would not give the plugin a sound output device. Nothing about the file is wrong.

sound.problem.directory.message: That is a folder, not a sound file.
sound.problem.directory.description: The path points at a folder rather than at a file. Worth keeping distinct from the missing-file message: the player can see the folder is there, so being told it is missing would send them looking in the wrong place.

sound.problem.format.message: Only .wav and .mp3 files can be played.
sound.problem.format.description: The chosen file is not one the plugin can play. ".wav" and ".mp3" are file extensions and stay as they are.

sound.problem.huge.message: That file is far larger than a notification sound should be, so it is being left alone.
sound.problem.huge.description: The file is far too large to be a notification sound, so the plugin will not open it. It is guarding against a video or a disk image typed in by mistake.

sound.problem.locked.message: That file could not be opened. Another program may have it open.
sound.problem.locked.description: The file exists but could not be opened, usually because another program has it open or Windows will not grant access.

sound.problem.missing.message: There is no file at that path any more.
sound.problem.missing.description: There is nothing at that path. "any more" because the path was picked at some point, so the file has usually been moved or deleted since.

sound.problem.none.message: No sound file has been chosen yet.
sound.problem.none.description: Shown when the file source is selected but no file has been picked. Not an error, just a step not done yet.

sound.problem.unreadable.description: The text in the box is not a path Windows will accept at all, for instance because of characters that cannot appear in a filename.

sound.silent.disabled.message: The game's sound is turned off, so nothing is played.
sound.silent.disabled.description: Shown when the game's own sound is switched off entirely, so pressing Play does nothing. It explains a silent button rather than reporting a fault.

sound.silent.muted.message: The game is muted, so nothing is played. This follows the master and System Sounds mute settings, because that is the bus a notification sound uses.
sound.silent.muted.description: Shown when the game is muted. "System Sounds" is a slider and a mute checkbox on the game's own sound settings screen: use the label your client shows, because naming the wrong one sends the player to a setting that will not help.

sound.silent.unfocused.message: The game window is not in front and its setting for playing sound while it is not active is off, so nothing is played.
sound.silent.unfocused.description: Shown when the game window is not in front and the game is set not to play sound then. The setting is on the game's own sound settings screen and is usually worded as playing sounds while the window is inactive.

sound.silent.unreadable.message: The game's sound settings cannot be read yet, so nothing is played. This clears once you are in game.
sound.silent.unreadable.description: Shown before the game's settings can be read, which in practice means at the title or character select screen.

sound.silent.zero.message: The game's master or System Sounds volume is at zero, so nothing is played.
sound.silent.zero.description: Shown when a volume slider is at zero rather than muted. "System Sounds" is a slider on the game's own sound settings screen, as above.

sound.problem.encoding.message: This file is a WAV in the {0} encoding, and Windows has no converter for it. Saving it again as ordinary PCM, or as an MP3, will work.
sound.problem.encoding.description: The WAV holds audio in a compressed or companded encoding and Windows has no converter installed for it. {0} is an encoding name from NAudio, in English, such as Adpcm, MuLaw or Gsm610: leave it as it is.

sound.problem.mp3codec.message: Windows has no MP3 decoder available, so this file cannot be played. A .wav file will still work.
sound.problem.mp3codec.description: Windows itself has no MP3 decoder available. Nothing about the file is wrong, which is why the message points at a .wav as the way round it. ".wav" is a file extension and stays as it is.

sound.problem.notaudio.message: That file is not really a WAV or an MP3, whatever its name says.
sound.problem.notaudio.description: The file has a .wav or .mp3 name but its contents are neither: no RIFF header, or no MP3 frames. Distinct from the damaged case, because the fix is to check which file was picked rather than to re-save it.

sound.problem.samples.message: That file is in a form the plugin cannot turn into sound. Saving it again as ordinary 16 bit PCM will work.
sound.problem.samples.description: The file is a WAV in a bit depth the plugin cannot turn into samples. It should not normally be reachable, so keep it plain and actionable rather than technical.

sound.problem.truncated.message: That file stops part way through and could not be read to the end.
sound.problem.truncated.description: The file ends part way through, so it was cut off in a download or a copy.

about.language.tooltip.message:
Follow Dalamud takes whichever language Dalamud itself is set to, and
changes with it.

Only this window is affected. Place and weather names come from the game
and stay in whatever language your client is running in.

announcements.bannergap.tooltip.message:
How far below a place name a banner sits, measured in lines of the
display text.

The two can be on screen together: entering a duty announces where you
are and then the party size a moment later. This is the room between
them. The drop is the same whether or not a name is up, so a banner on
its own also lands here.

announcements.bannerlanguage.tooltip.message:
Which language the banner wording is drawn in.

Following the client uses the language the game is in. Choosing another replaces the game's own banner with this plugin's version in that language, so on a German client set to English the German artwork is faded out and English words are drawn in its place.

Only languages this plugin has wording for are listed. Banners it has no wording for keep the game's own, whichever language is chosen.

announcements.banners.tooltip.message:
Redraws the game's full-screen banners ("Quest Accepted", "Duty Commenced", "Level Up!") in this plugin's lettering.

The wording is painted into the game's artwork rather than stored as text, so only banners this plugin has words for are taken over. Any it does not recognise keep the game's own.

announcements.hideareatext.message: Hide the game's own area text

announcements.hideareatext.tooltip.message: Suppresses the native "_AreaText" flash, which draws underneath this plugin.

announcements.hidebanner.tooltip.message:
Fades out the game's artwork so only this plugin's version shows.

Turn this off to see both, which is a quick way to check the wording matches.

announcements.hideloadingtitle.tooltip.message:
Suppresses "_LocationTitle" and "_LocationTitleShort", the gold title
drawn over the loading screen, and shows the same names in this
plugin's style instead.

announcements.intro.message: This plugin replaces the game's own location text rather than drawing alongside it. If you turn the suppression below off, the game's version comes back.

announcements.skipfast.tooltip.message:
Only affects sub-areas, and only above a speed no ground travel reaches,
so it comes into play when flying. Zone and area changes are always
announced however fast you are moving.

announcements.tab.description: Tab label. What the plugin says out loud: which place tiers, the weather, the banners, and when to stay quiet. Tab labels sit in one row, so shorter is better where the language allows it.

announcements.weather.tooltip.message:
Announces the weather turning over, on its own line just above the place name, so it never interrupts a location notice.

Weather runs on a fixed cycle of about 23 minutes, and arriving anywhere new announces what it is doing there, so it shows up with the place name as you walk in.

announcements.weathericon.tooltip.message: Draws the game's own icon for the weather to the left of its name.

appearance.headergap.tooltip.message:
How far the name sits below the header, measured in lines of header text.

Low values pull the two together until they almost touch, which is the
tighter look the plugin has always shipped with. Higher values open the
gap up and give each line room to breathe.

appearance.horizontal.tooltip.message:
The text is centred on this point, so 50% is the middle of the screen.
A long place name set near either end will reach past it.

appearance.letterspacing.tooltip.message:
Extra space between letters, as a percentage of the font size, so it keeps
its proportions when the size changes and the header gets its own share.
Wide spacing is much of what gives the Guild Wars 2 original its look.

appearance.separatecolours.tooltip.message:
Off, the weather line follows the header, and one outline colour
covers all three lines.

On, the weather line and the outlines take the colours below, so one
line can be pushed towards the background without touching the others.

appearance.shadow.tooltip.message:
A second copy of every line, offset behind it. Sits under the outline, so
the two can be used together: a tight outline for legibility and a soft
shadow for depth.

One shadow covers all three lines; it does not follow the separate colours.

appearance.shadowacross.tooltip.message: Negative moves the shadow to the left.

appearance.shadowdown.tooltip.message: Negative lifts the shadow above the text.

appearance.shadowspread.tooltip.message:
Fattens the shadow outwards. Zero keeps it the same shape as the
letters; higher values thicken it into a halo behind them.

appearance.showheader.tooltip.message:
The smaller line above the name, giving where the place sits: the region
above a zone, the area above a sub-area.

Turned off, only the name itself is shown. The weather line, if you have
it on, is unaffected, as are the two settings below, which still apply
to it.

appearance.tab.description: Tab label. How a notification looks: where it sits, its colours, outline, shadow and header. Keep it short.

motion.choice.intro.message: How the letters move as they arrive.

motion.choice.tooltip.message:
None: the letters simply appear where they belong.
Typewriter: one letter at a time, no fade.
Rise: letters lift into place from below.
Wave: letters ride a wave through the line as it appears.
Burn: letters catch alight and cool into their colour.

Runs alongside the Eorzean decode rather than instead of it.

motion.decode.duration.description: Slider label, directly under the decode checkbox. Reads as a length of time rather than as a repeat of the checkbox above it.

motion.decode.duration.tooltip.message:
How long the Eorzean takes to resolve, once the letters have landed.
Needs the decode effect above.
motion.decode.duration.tooltip.description: Tooltip for that slider. "Eorzean" is the game's invented script.

motion.decode.tooltip.message:
Requires a bundled Eorzean font. Latin text only.

Runs after the motion above rather than alongside it: the line
arrives in Eorzean, lands, then resolves. Turned off, it arrives
already readable. Presets leave this alone, so switching it off
here switches it off for all of them.
motion.decode.tooltip.description: Tooltip for the Eorzean decode checkbox. "Presets" is the name of another tab. It used to say the motion was on the Effects tab; the two are now next to each other, which is why it says "above".

motion.duration.description: Slider label, directly under the Motion dropdown. It was "Motion" on a tab of its own until the two were put together, and needs to read as a length of time rather than as a second copy of the dropdown above it.

motion.duration.tooltip.message:
How long the letters take to arrive. Runs alongside the fade in, and
does nothing when the motion above is None.
motion.duration.tooltip.description: Tooltip for that slider. "None" is an entry in the Motion dropdown above it - match motion.choice.none.

motion.embers.note.message: Embers go with the Burn motion, but they do not need it.

motion.fadein.tooltip.message: How long the line takes to come up to full strength as it appears.

motion.fadeout.tooltip.message: How long the line takes to disappear once its time is up.

motion.hold.tooltip.message: How long the finished line stays up before it starts to fade.

motion.intro.message: The line arrives, lands, then decodes. Motion and decode are separate stages and each takes its own time.

motion.particlecolour.tooltip.message:
The default amber suits embers and sparkles. Hearts and petals
want moving towards pink.

motion.particles.intro.message: What plays around it, for as long as it is on screen.

motion.tab.description: Tab label. How a notification moves: the arrival effect, the Eorzean decode, particles and the timings. Keep it short.

motion.timing.intro.message: How long the whole notification lasts, whichever of the above it is using.
motion.timing.intro.description: Greyed heading over the last three sliders on the Motion tab, which apply whatever arrival effect is chosen above them.

sound.audition.tooltip.message: Plays the chosen sound now. It ignores the short gap that stops two notifications sounding at once, so pressing it repeatedly always makes a noise.

sound.intro.message: A short noise when a notification arrives, from the game's own sound effects or from a file of your own.
sound.intro.description: Paragraph at the top of the Sound tab.

sound.on.tooltip.message: Which kinds of notification make a sound. Two arriving together only ever make one sound, whichever of them lands first.

sound.source.tooltip.message:
Plays a sound when a notification appears. Off by default.

One of the game's is a chat sound effect, mixed by the game: the master volume and the System Sounds volume control it, rather than Sound Effects, and turning Sound Effects down will not quieten it.

A file of your own is played by the plugin, which the game does not mix at all, so the plugin reads those same settings and follows them by hand. It stays silent while the game is muted, and while the window is not in front unless you have told the game to keep playing then.

sound.tab.description: Tab label. The noise a notification makes. Keep it short.
